title: Panorama batch orchestrator and tail safeguard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a low-risk runtime component (Panorama) that observes stream-level signals and applies coordinated admission shaping, short-term kernel hints, and tail-protection policies.

Motivation: Current continuous batching suffers sporadic tail spikes when heterogeneous sequences and multi-tenant bursts combine. We need a lightweight orchestrator that can:
- synthesize per-request signals (sequence length, requested max_tokens, user SLAs, tenancy tag)
- steer admission decisions (early deferral vs immediate scheduling) and batch shape (splitting vs coalescing)
- emit kernel preference hints for the kernel selector to prefer smaller-memory/low-latency kernels when tail risk is detected

Key constraints:
- Must add <5% median overhead to admission path
- Work within existing RPC and admission APIs (no large refactor)
- Needs to be compatible with Dedicated pools and Private deployments (no external telemetry reliance)

Success metrics (measured on canary traffic):
- 95th percentile token latency reduction >= 20% on mixed-tenant workloads
- No more than 3% degradation to average token throughput
- Observability: expose per-route tail-risk score and kernel-hint distribution in Console

Out-of-scope: global autoscaling controls, long-term historical ML predictors (we'll integrate later in a separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Panorama module implemented as a pluggable admission filter and enabled behind a feature flag
Admission decisions annotated with tail-risk score and kernel_hint tag (lowmem | balanced | throughput)
Kernel selector consumes kernel_hint and prefers compatible kernels when available
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating 95th percentile latency reduction on the mixed-tenant synthetic workload
Console dashboard tile showing tail-risk heatmap and kernel-hint breakdown per model/route

comments: 2026-02-21 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff sync with runtime and kernel teams. Agreed to keep signal extractor purely in-memory; no external calls. Decided on three kernel_hint buckets to minimize selector complexity.

2026-02-25 — Marco Ruiz: Drafted API sketch for admission annotations and added it to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Panorama+Design. Please review the kernel_hint enum and scoring range.

2026-03-01 — Chen Li: Implemented prototype signal extractor. Early perf numbers show ~2.1% median overhead on microbenchmarks. Observed that short sequences (<12 tokens) often get misclassified; added length-normalization in scoring.

2026-03-03 — Priya Desai: Kernel selector PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427. The selector honors kernel_hint when compatibility table has matching kernels; fallback to existing ranking otherwise. Needs perf review.

2026-03-05 — Olivia Morgan: Console mockups uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1PanoramaUI. Dashboard will have heatmap + per-route explanatory tooltip. UX review requested from PM and SRE.

2026-03-08 — SRE (K. Nguyen): Canary plan drafted. We'll run mixed-tenant bursts with 5K requests/s for 30 minutes. Need gating criteria for rollback (95th latency > baseline by 15% or error rate > 0.5%).

2026-03-09 — Marco Ruiz: After perf pass on selector, we reduced compatibility checks by caching kernel capability masks per-model which cut decision latency by ~0.6ms. Added a stress test to CI to ensure cache invalidation correctness.

2026-03-10 — Product (Leah Carter): Reviewed trade-offs. Concern: too aggressive kernel_hint could worsen throughput for batch-friendly workloads. Agreed to implement conservative tuning default and expose knob per-customer via Dedicated config.

2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Next steps: finish telemetry wiring, finalize canary dataset, and prepare postmortem playbook for canary rollback. Assigned QA to run regression suite on runtime-1.20 branch.
